We need to return all possible precursors of applying the template (template_id 1679747) to the target molecule (initial_molecule SMILES: C=C(C1=CC=C(OC)C=C1)C2=CC=C(OC)C=C2). The template is given as mapped_rxn: "O=[C:2]([c:3]1[cH:4][cH:5][c:6]([O:7][CH3:8])[cH:9][cH:10]1)[c:11]1[cH:12][cH:13][c:14]([O:15][CH3:16])[cH:17][cH:18]1.[Li][CH2:1][Si](C)(C)C>>[CH2:1]=[C:2]([c:3]1[cH:4][cH:5][c:6]([O:7][CH3:8])[cH:9][cH:10]1)[c:11]1[cH:12][cH:13][c:14]([O:15][CH3:16])[cH:17][cH:18]1"

So forward reaction: a carbonyl (O= C) attached to aromatic rings (two phenyl groups with OMe substituents) plus LiCH2Si(C)(C)C (a silyl carbanion) gives alkene product: CH2= C(aryl1)(aryl2). So retrosynthetic step: break the C=C double bond to give a carbonyl (ketone) and a silyl carbanion (LiCH2SiMe3). The target molecule is a stilbene derivative with two anisole rings (methoxy phenyl). The product SMILES: C=C(C1=CC=C(OC)C=C1)C2=CC=C(OC)C=C2. That's exactly the product.

Thus applying template retrosynthetically should give precursors: a ketone: O= C(aryl1)(aryl2) (i.e., a diaryl ketone) and LiCH2SiMe3 (or maybe LiCH2Si(C)(C)C). The template likely expects the silyl carbanion as [Li][CH2:1][Si](C)(C)C. So we need to output SMILES strings for each precursor.

We need to apply the template to the target molecule using apply_template tool to get all possible precursors. Let's do that.
